//! A streamed chat reply, built part by part instead of whole on every chunk.
//!
//! [`StreamingDoc`] keeps the top-level blocks of the reply that cannot change any more as
//! frozen [`Segment`]s, and parses only the rest, the tail, on each chunk. The tree it returns
//! is the one [`build`] gives for the same text: Markdown reads some blocks by what stands
//! elsewhere in the reply, so a block is frozen only where that cannot differ, and the parts that
//! can are built again together (a rewind) or never frozen apart (a hold).
//!
//! What a block can depend on beyond itself, and what is done about it:
//!
//! - **A link or footnote definition.** The references it answers read it wherever it stands.
//!   Every part that writes `[label` for a defined label stays in one parse: a definition that
//!   arrives after a frozen reference rewinds to it, a reference after a frozen definition
//!   rewinds to the definition, and no cut falls between the first and the last mention.
//! - **Footnote numbers.** Ely numbers a footnote by its first reference in the reply, so a part
//!   would number from one: once a frozen segment holds a reference, a reference in the tail
//!   rewinds to it, and no cut falls between two references.
//! - **`$$` pairs.** Ely pairs every run of two dollars outside code with the next one, from the
//!   top of the reply, and a fence pair is a math block across the blocks between. The cut never
//!   falls inside a pair, nor passes a run that is still waiting for its partner.
//! - **Block HTML room.** It is the cap less the deepest Markdown of the whole reply. Each
//!   segment keeps the deepest it was built under, and is built again when that changes.
//! - **A block start that a line to come can undo.** A block that starts right under a line of
//!   text is told by the lines after it (a table needs its delimiter row, a definition goes on
//!   over its title), and what the text above is changes with them. After a blank line a block
//!   starts whatever follows, but the line it starts on may still change under it: `2` is a
//!   paragraph, `2.` the next item of the list above (`#` and then `#tag` too). So a cut falls
//!   only before a block that follows a blank line, and not on the line being written.
//! - **A byte order mark.** Ely drops one from the start of the text it reads and keeps any
//!   other as text, so no part starts at one except the first.
//! - **The nesting cap.** A part the guard refuses makes the whole reply one plain paragraph, as
//!   [`build`] does: from then on every chunk is a full build.
//!
//! `\(` pairs read inside one paragraph, heading or table cell, so they cross no block.

use std::borrow::Cow;
use std::ops::Range;
use std::rc::Rc;

use ely_gpui_component::documents::{MarkdownBlock, markdown_options};
use pulldown_cmark::{Event, LinkType, Options, Parser, Tag, TagEnd};

use super::{MarkdownBlocks, Parts, Policy, Within, build, join, parts, rewrite};
use crate::markdown_preview::DiagramRequest;

/// Moves every source offset the tree keeps by `by`, wrapping: the first byte of the part it was
/// built from, in the reply it is a part of. `Code.from`, `Image.at` and the spans of an
/// inline's pieces count bytes of the source Ely read, and Ely read the part alone.
pub(super) fn shift(nodes: &mut [MarkdownBlock], by: usize) {
    if by == 0 {
        return;
    }
    rewrite::each_mut(nodes, &mut |node| match node {
        MarkdownBlock::Paragraph(inline) | MarkdownBlock::Heading(_, inline) => {
            for (_, span, _) in &mut inline.sources {
                *span = span.start.wrapping_add(by)..span.end.wrapping_add(by);
            }
        }
        MarkdownBlock::Code { from, .. } => *from = from.wrapping_add(by),
        MarkdownBlock::Image { at, .. } => *at = at.wrapping_add(by),
        _ => {}
    });
}

/// A definition's label, and how a reference writes it.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct Label {
    name: String,
    /// A footnote, written `[^name]`; else a link reference, `[name]`.
    note: bool,
}

impl Label {
    /// The first and the last place `text` writes `[` and this label, if it does. Case does not
    /// tell labels apart, nor does the width of a run of white space; the labels of other
    /// scripts fold by rules that are not ours, so any bracket may name one. Whatever follows
    /// the label is not looked at: a longer word over-matches, which only keeps parts together.
    fn mentions(&self, text: &str) -> Option<(usize, usize)> {
        let mut found: Option<(usize, usize)> = None;
        for (at, _) in text.match_indices('[') {
            if self.names(&text[at + 1..]) {
                found = Some(found.map_or((at, at), |(first, _)| (first, at)));
            }
        }
        found
    }

    /// Whether `rest`, what follows a `[`, starts with this label.
    fn names(&self, rest: &str) -> bool {
        let rest = match (self.note, rest.strip_prefix('^')) {
            (false, _) => rest,
            (true, Some(rest)) => rest,
            (true, None) => return false,
        };
        // A reference may pad its label: the white space at both ends is not part of it.
        let rest = rest.trim_start_matches(char::is_whitespace);
        if !self.name.is_ascii() {
            return true;
        }
        let mut text = rest.chars().peekable();
        let mut label = self.name.chars().peekable();
        while let Some(wanted) = label.next() {
            if wanted.is_whitespace() {
                while label.peek().is_some_and(|next| next.is_whitespace()) {
                    label.next();
                }
                if !text.next().is_some_and(char::is_whitespace) {
                    return false;
                }
                while text.peek().is_some_and(|next| next.is_whitespace()) {
                    text.next();
                }
            } else {
                match text.next() {
                    None => return false,
                    // Case folding writes some ASCII letters in other scripts (`ß` is `ss`).
                    Some(found) if !found.is_ascii() => return true,
                    Some(found) if !found.eq_ignore_ascii_case(&wanted) => return false,
                    Some(_) => {}
                }
            }
        }
        true
    }
}

/// What one pass over the text Ely read says of its blocks.
#[derive(Default)]
struct Scan {
    /// Where each top-level block starts, in bytes of that text.
    starts: Vec<usize>,
    /// The labels it defines, links and footnotes.
    labels: Vec<Label>,
    /// Where it writes a footnote reference.
    notes: Vec<usize>,
}

impl Scan {
    fn of(read: &str) -> Self {
        let mut found = Self::default();
        let mut depth = 0usize;
        let mut events = Parser::new_ext(read, markdown_options()).into_offset_iter();
        for (event, range) in events.by_ref() {
            match event {
                Event::Start(tag) => {
                    if depth == 0 {
                        found.starts.push(range.start);
                    }
                    if let Tag::FootnoteDefinition(name) = &tag {
                        found.labels.push(Label {
                            name: name.to_string(),
                            note: true,
                        });
                    }
                    depth += 1;
                }
                Event::End(_) => depth = depth.saturating_sub(1),
                Event::Rule if depth == 0 => found.starts.push(range.start),
                Event::FootnoteReference(_) => found.notes.push(range.start),
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        for (name, _) in events.reference_definitions().iter() {
            found.labels.push(Label {
                name: name.to_owned(),
                note: false,
            });
        }
        found
    }
}

/// Where the text Ely read stands in the source it read: a byte order mark is dropped, a lone CR
/// is a line end of the same width, and a `$$` fence is a run of tildes one longer. An offset
/// inside a fence, or after text that reads otherwise, maps nowhere.
struct Alignment {
    /// A stretch of the read text, and where it starts in the source.
    pieces: Vec<(Range<usize>, usize)>,
}

impl Alignment {
    fn of(read: &str, source: &str) -> Self {
        let bom = if source.starts_with('\u{feff}') { '\u{feff}'.len_utf8() } else { 0 };
        let (read, written) = (read.as_bytes(), &source.as_bytes()[bom..]);
        let (mut i, mut j) = (0, 0);
        let (mut from_i, mut from_j) = (0, 0);
        let mut pieces = Vec::new();
        loop {
            while i < read.len()
                && j < written.len()
                && (read[i] == written[j]
                    || (read[i] == b'\n'
                        && written[j] == b'\r'
                        && written.get(j + 1) != Some(&b'\n')))
            {
                i += 1;
                j += 1;
            }
            pieces.push((from_i..i, from_j + bom));
            let dollars = written[j..].iter().take_while(|byte| **byte == b'$').count();
            let tildes = read[i..].iter().take_while(|byte| **byte == b'~').count();
            if dollars < 2 || tildes != dollars + 1 {
                break;
            }
            (i, j) = (i + tildes, j + dollars);
            (from_i, from_j) = (i, j);
        }
        Self { pieces }
    }

    fn map(&self, at: usize) -> Option<usize> {
        (self.pieces.iter())
            .find(|(read, _)| read.start <= at && at <= read.end)
            .map(|(read, source)| source + at - read.start)
    }
}

/// Where the line holding byte `at` of `text` starts: a block never starts after the indent or
/// the marker of its own line, and a part that did would read an indented code block as a
/// paragraph.
fn line_start(text: &str, at: usize) -> usize {
    text[..at].rfind(['\n', '\r']).map_or(0, |end| end + 1)
}

/// Where the `$$` runs of a text pair. Ely pairs them from the top of the reply: every run of
/// two dollars or more outside code takes the next as long (Ely's `flow::paired`), whatever
/// stands between the two.
#[derive(Default)]
struct Dollars {
    /// Each pair, from the first byte of its opening run to the last of its closing one.
    pairs: Vec<Range<usize>>,
    /// The first run that has no partner yet.
    open: Option<usize>,
}

impl Dollars {
    fn of(text: &str) -> Self {
        let mut found = Self::default();
        if !text.contains("$$") {
            return found;
        }
        let text = lone_crs_as_lf(text);
        let held = not_prose(&text);
        let bytes = text.as_bytes();
        let mut at = 0;
        while let Some(open) = next_run(bytes, at, 2, &held) {
            match next_run(bytes, open.end, open.len(), &held) {
                Some(close) => {
                    found.pairs.push(open.start..close.end);
                    at = close.end;
                }
                None => {
                    found.open = Some(open.start);
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
        found
    }

    /// Whether a part may start at byte `at`. A pair is settled whole: a part that starts
    /// between its runs would pair them with others. A run that has no partner yet may take one
    /// that arrives, and everything after it with it.
    fn allows(&self, at: usize) -> bool {
        self.open.is_none_or(|open| at <= open)
            && !self.pairs.iter().any(|pair| pair.start < at && at < pair.end)
    }
}

/// Whether the line before the one that starts at byte `at` of `text` (a line start after the
/// first) is blank. A block that follows a blank line starts there whatever the lines after it
/// say; under a line of text it starts only if they say so.
fn after_blank_line(text: &str, at: usize) -> bool {
    let before = &text[..at];
    let before = (before.strip_suffix("\r\n"))
        .or_else(|| before.strip_suffix(['\n', '\r']))
        .unwrap_or(before);
    let line = &before[before.rfind(['\n', '\r']).map_or(0, |end| end + 1)..];
    line.bytes().all(|byte| matches!(byte, b' ' | b'\t'))
}

/// `text` with each lone CR as LF: what pulldown-cmark ends a line at, of the same width.
fn lone_crs_as_lf(text: &str) -> Cow<'_, str> {
    if !text.contains('\r') {
        return Cow::Borrowed(text);
    }
    let mut bytes = text.as_bytes().to_vec();
    for at in 0..bytes.len() {
        if bytes[at] == b'\r' && bytes.get(at + 1) != Some(&b'\n') {
            bytes[at] = b'\n';
        }
    }
    Cow::Owned(String::from_utf8(bytes).expect("LF for CR keeps UTF-8"))
}

/// All but prose, as the text reads without math: code, HTML, link targets (Ely's
/// `flow::not_prose`, which `$$` runs are not paired inside).
fn not_prose(text: &str) -> Vec<Range<usize>> {
    let mut held = Vec::new();
    let (mut at, mut quiet) = (0, 0usize);
    let mut links = Vec::new();
    let plain = markdown_options().difference(Options::ENABLE_MATH);
    for (event, range) in Parser::new_ext(text, plain).into_offset_iter() {
        match event {
            Event::Start(Tag::CodeBlock(_) | Tag::MetadataBlock(_) | Tag::Image { .. }) => {
                quiet += 1;
            }
            Event::End(TagEnd::CodeBlock | TagEnd::MetadataBlock(_) | TagEnd::Image) => {
                quiet = quiet.saturating_sub(1);
            }
            Event::Start(Tag::Link { link_type, .. }) => {
                let auto = matches!(link_type, LinkType::Autolink | LinkType::Email);
                quiet += usize::from(auto);
                links.push(auto);
            }
            Event::End(TagEnd::Link) => {
                quiet = quiet.saturating_sub(usize::from(links.pop() == Some(true)));
            }
            Event::Text(_) if quiet == 0 && range.start >= at => {
                held.push(at..range.start);
                at = range.end;
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    held.push(at..text.len());
    held.retain(|gap| !gap.is_empty());
    held
}

/// The first run of at least `len` dollars from byte `from`, outside `held`.
fn next_run(
    bytes: &[u8],
    from: usize,
    len: usize,
    held: &[Range<usize>],
) -> Option<Range<usize>> {
    let mut at = from;
    while at < bytes.len() {
        if let Some(block) = held.iter().find(|block| block.contains(&at)) {
            at = block.end;
            continue;
        }
        let run = bytes[at..].iter().take_while(|byte| **byte == b'$').count();
        if run >= len {
            return Some(at..at + run);
        }
        at += run.max(1);
    }
    None
}

/// One frozen stretch of the reply and the nodes built for exactly that stretch.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub(crate) struct Segment {
    pub range: Range<usize>,
    pub nodes: Rc<[MarkdownBlock]>,
    /// Block HTML was read in it, so the Markdown depth of the reply decided its room.
    pub has_block_html: bool,
    missing: Rc<[DiagramRequest]>,
    /// The deepest nesting of its own Markdown.
    deepest: usize,
    /// The deepest of the whole reply when it was built: what its block HTML had room for.
    room: usize,
    /// The labels it defines.
    labels: Vec<Label>,
    /// Whether it writes a footnote reference.
    notes: bool,
}

/// A reply that streams in, built part by part. `text` only grows between two calls of
/// [`update`](Self::update); a text that does not start with the bytes frozen so far is no
/// continuation of the reply, and starts over.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub(crate) struct StreamingDoc {
    /// Everything before it is frozen: the segments tile `text[..cut]`.
    cut: usize,
    segments: Vec<Segment>,
    /// The bytes frozen, `text[..cut]`: what a text must start with to continue the reply.
    frozen: String,
    /// The nesting guard refused a part: every build is a build of the whole reply.
    whole: bool,
}

impl StreamingDoc {
    pub(crate) fn new() -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }

    // The next three are read by the tests now, and by the reveal (a later task of this
    // delivery) once it draws a reply by its parts.
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    pub(crate) fn segments(&self) -> &[Segment] {
        &self.segments
    }

    #[allow(dead_code)]
    pub(crate) fn cut(&self) -> usize {
        self.cut
    }

    #[allow(dead_code)]
    pub(crate) fn is_whole(&self) -> bool {
        self.whole
    }

    /// The tree of `text`, the reply so far: what [`build`] returns for it.
    pub(crate) fn update(&mut self, text: &str, policy: &mut Policy<'_>) -> MarkdownBlocks {
        if !text.starts_with(&self.frozen) {
            *self = Self::new();
        }
        if self.whole {
            return build(text, policy);
        }
        let (mut tail, read, scan) = loop {
            let mut tail = parts(
                &text[self.cut..],
                policy,
                Within {
                    deepest: self.deepest(),
                    offset: self.cut,
                },
                true,
            );
            if tail.refused || tail.declined {
                self.whole = true;
                return build(text, policy);
            }
            let read = tail.read.take().unwrap_or_default();
            let scan = Scan::of(&read);
            match self.rewind_from(text, &tail, &scan) {
                Some(index) => self.truncate(index),
                None => break (tail, read, scan),
            }
        };
        let deepest = self.deepest().max(tail.deepest);
        let mut missing: Vec<DiagramRequest> = Vec::new();
        let wanted = self.segments.iter().flat_map(|segment| segment.missing.iter());
        for request in wanted.chain(tail.missing.iter()) {
            if !missing.iter().any(|known| known.key == request.key) {
                missing.push(request.clone());
            }
        }
        let mut nodes = Vec::new();
        for segment in &self.segments {
            nodes.extend(segment.nodes.iter().cloned());
        }
        nodes.append(&mut tail.nodes);
        let document = join(nodes, missing);
        self.freeze(text, &read, &scan, deepest, policy);
        document
    }

    /// The deepest nesting of the Markdown of the frozen segments.
    fn deepest(&self) -> usize {
        (self.segments.iter())
            .map(|segment| segment.deepest)
            .max()
            .unwrap_or(0)
    }

    /// Frozen segments back to `index` become tail again.
    fn truncate(&mut self, index: usize) {
        self.cut = self.segments[index].range.start;
        self.segments.truncate(index);
        self.frozen.truncate(self.cut);
    }

    /// The first frozen segment the tail makes wrong, if there is one.
    fn rewind_from(&self, text: &str, tail: &Parts, scan: &Scan) -> Option<usize> {
        let mut first: Option<usize> = None;
        let mut note = |index: usize| first = Some(first.map_or(index, |known| known.min(index)));
        let source = |segment: &Segment| &text[segment.range.clone()];

        // Block HTML took its room from another depth than the reply has now.
        let reply = self.deepest().max(tail.deepest);
        if let Some(index) = (self.segments.iter())
            .position(|segment| segment.has_block_html && segment.room != reply)
        {
            note(index);
        }

        // A label written in the tail, and in a frozen part too: one parse, or the reference
        // and the definition may not meet.
        let tail_source = &text[self.cut..];
        let frozen = self.segments.iter().flat_map(|segment| segment.labels.iter());
        for label in frozen.chain(scan.labels.iter()) {
            if label.mentions(tail_source).is_none() {
                continue;
            }
            if let Some(index) = (self.segments.iter())
                .position(|segment| label.mentions(source(segment)).is_some())
            {
                note(index);
            }
        }

        // Footnotes number from the first reference of the reply, not of the part.
        if !scan.notes.is_empty()
            && let Some(index) = self.segments.iter().position(|segment| segment.notes)
        {
            note(index);
        }
        first
    }

    /// Freezes what can no longer change: every block before the last that can be left alone.
    fn freeze(
        &mut self,
        text: &str,
        read: &str,
        scan: &Scan,
        deepest: usize,
        policy: &mut Policy<'_>,
    ) {
        let tail = &text[self.cut..];
        let alignment = Alignment::of(read, tail);

        // Where a part may start: a line that starts a top-level block, mapped back to the source.
        let mut starts: Vec<usize> = (scan.starts.iter())
            .filter_map(|at| alignment.map(*at))
            .map(|at| line_start(tail, at))
            .filter(|at| *at > 0)
            .collect();
        starts.dedup();
        // Between the first and the last place a defined label is written, a cut would part a
        // reference from its definition. Between two footnote references it would number the
        // second from one. Inside a `$$` pair, or past a run that waits for a partner, it would
        // pair the runs after it elsewhere.
        let mut spans: Vec<(usize, usize)> = (scan.labels.iter())
            .filter_map(|label| label.mentions(tail))
            .collect();
        let notes: Vec<usize> = (scan.notes.iter())
            .map(|at| alignment.map(*at).unwrap_or(usize::MAX))
            .collect();
        if let (Some(first), Some(last)) = (notes.iter().min(), notes.iter().max()) {
            spans.push((*first, *last));
        }
        let dollars = Dollars::of(tail);
        // The line being written: the block that starts on it may be none once it is done, or
        // taken up by the block above (`#` and `#tag`, `2` and `2.` after a list item).
        let unfinished = (!tail.ends_with(['\n', '\r'])).then(|| line_start(tail, tail.len()));
        starts.retain(|at| {
            after_blank_line(tail, *at)
                && Some(*at) != unfinished
                && !tail[*at..].starts_with('\u{feff}')
                && dollars.allows(*at)
                && !spans.iter().any(|(first, last)| first < at && at <= last)
        });

        let mut from = 0;
        for at in starts {
            let range = self.cut + from..self.cut + at;
            let made = parts(
                &text[range.clone()],
                policy,
                Within {
                    deepest,
                    offset: range.start,
                },
                true,
            );
            if made.refused || made.declined {
                // The segments made so far stay: they tile the text up to the cut.
                self.whole = true;
                break;
            }
            let own = Scan::of(made.read.as_deref().unwrap_or_default());
            self.segments.push(Segment {
                range,
                nodes: Rc::from(made.nodes),
                has_block_html: made.block_html,
                missing: Rc::from(made.missing),
                deepest: made.deepest,
                room: deepest.max(made.deepest),
                labels: own.labels,
                notes: !own.notes.is_empty(),
            });
            from = at;
        }
        self.frozen.push_str(&text[self.cut..self.cut + from]);
        self.cut += from;
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
#[path = "stream_tests.rs"]
mod stream_tests;
//! Markdown, parsed once with Ely's reader and rewritten for the surface that shows it.
//!
//! [`build`] reads a source into Ely's tree, then rewrites it by what the surface lets
//! through (pictures, links, diagrams, block HTML), and keeps beside it what selection,
//! copy and the anchors need: the plain text, the headings and their slugs.

use std::cell::Cell;
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::path::Path;
use std::rc::Rc;

use ely_gpui_component::documents::{
    MarkdownBlock, Style, markdown_options, parse_markdown_guarded,
};
use gpui::SharedString;
use pulldown_cmark::{Event, Parser};

use crate::chat::file_links::FileLinkMemo;
use crate::markdown_preview::{DiagramRequest, Diagrams};

mod code;
pub(crate) mod cull;
mod gather;
mod menu;
mod rewrite;
mod sideways;
mod slug;
mod stream;
mod text;
mod view;

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests;

pub(crate) use gather::BodyLayouts;
#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) use gather::DrawnPart;
pub(crate) use menu::{MarkdownMenuItem, perform};
pub(crate) use slug::slug;
pub(crate) use stream::StreamingDoc;
pub(crate) use text::{PartKind, PlainText};
pub(crate) use view::{
    BodyActions, LinkHandler, MarkdownView, MenuHandler, MenuPress, SelectionHost, ViewFlags,
    markdown_view, probe_view,
};

/// The deepest nesting drawn as written; past it the source is one plain paragraph. Ely's
/// reader, its element builder and gpui's layout recurse once per level, a level costs about
/// 115 KiB of stack in a debug build, and the cap must fit the smallest main thread: measured
/// by drawing quotes, lists and alerts, the deepest that draws is 71 levels in a release
/// build on 1 MiB (Windows) and 75 in a debug build on 8 MiB (Linux and macOS). The cap is
/// half the smaller of the two, rounded down to a multiple of 8, so the chat's extra wrappers
/// have room too. Real Markdown rarely nests past ten. A debug draw on 4 MiB (half of 8) and
/// a release one on 1 MiB (`the_deepest_allowed_nesting_is_drawn_on_a_four_mebibyte_stack`,
/// `..._on_a_release_one_mebibyte_stack`) go red when the cap is raised past that margin.
pub(crate) const MAX_NESTING: usize = 32;

/// The deepest block HTML is built: a reader sees nothing in more levels, and what is built
/// is walked, dropped and drawn by recursion on whatever stack the caller has.
pub(crate) const MAX_HTML_NESTING: usize = 32;

/// Who shows the document.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum Surface {
    Preview,
    Chat,
    ChangeRequest,
}

/// The diagram pipeline's state, borrowed from the file view that owns and changes it.
pub(crate) struct DiagramInputs<'a> {
    pub states: &'a Diagrams,
    pub palette: &'a sirio_diagram::Palette,
}

/// What finding the files a chat reply names takes: `link_file_paths`'s inputs.
pub(crate) struct FileLinkInputs<'a> {
    pub worktree: &'a Path,
    pub home: Option<&'a Path>,
    pub memo: &'a mut FileLinkMemo,
}

/// What a surface lets through.
pub(crate) struct Policy<'a> {
    pub surface: Surface,
    /// The file's folder (Preview) or the worktree (Chat). Sirio's own: Ely never gets it.
    pub base: Option<&'a Path>,
    pub diagrams: Option<DiagramInputs<'a>>,
    pub file_links: Option<FileLinkInputs<'a>>,
}

/// A heading of the final tree.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct Heading {
    /// The renderer's `heading-N`: the drawing order over the final tree.
    pub ordinal: usize,
    pub slug: SharedString,
    pub title: SharedString,
    pub depth: usize,
}

/// How many of each kind of node the tree holds.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct NodeCounts {
    pub math: usize,
    pub alerts: usize,
    pub footnotes: usize,
    pub images: usize,
    pub tables: usize,
    pub code: usize,
    /// Tables of contents turned into links.
    pub toc: usize,
}

/// A parsed document and what each surface needs beside it.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub(crate) struct MarkdownBlocks {
    pub nodes: Rc<[MarkdownBlock]>,
    pub text: Rc<PlainText>,
    pub headings: Rc<[Heading]>,
    /// Diagrams the tree names that nobody has scheduled yet.
    pub missing_diagrams: Vec<DiagramRequest>,
    pub kinds: NodeCounts,
}

impl std::fmt::Debug for MarkdownBlocks {
    /// What is drawn is not content a log should carry: the sizes only.
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("MarkdownBlocks")
            .field("nodes", &self.nodes.len())
            .field("bytes", &self.text.text.len())
            .finish()
    }
}

/// How deep `source`, the text Ely's parser reads, nests, or one past the cap when it nests
/// deeper. Ely's reader and its drawing recurse once per level, and chat and forge text is not
/// ours: this walks the event stream, which takes no stack, before any tree exists.
fn markdown_depth(source: &str) -> usize {
    let (mut depth, mut deepest) = (0usize, 0usize);
    for event in Parser::new_ext(source, markdown_options()) {
        match event {
            Event::Start(_) => {
                depth += 1;
                deepest = deepest.max(depth);
                if depth > MAX_NESTING {
                    return depth;
                }
            }
            Event::End(_) => depth = depth.saturating_sub(1),
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    deepest
}

/// How deep `nodes` nest, a leaf counting one.
fn tree_depth(nodes: &[MarkdownBlock]) -> usize {
    (nodes.iter())
        .map(|node| {
            let inner = (rewrite::bodies(node).into_iter())
                .map(tree_depth)
                .max()
                .unwrap_or(0);
            1 + inner
        })
        .max()
        .unwrap_or(0)
}

/// What the per-block half of [`build`] makes of one source: the nodes the surface draws, before
/// anything that looks across the whole reply (headings, tables of contents, counts, text).
pub(crate) struct Parts {
    pub nodes: Vec<MarkdownBlock>,
    pub missing: Vec<DiagramRequest>,
    /// The deepest nesting the guard accepted in any text Ely read for this source.
    pub deepest: usize,
    /// The guard refused the source (or block HTML made the tree too deep): `nodes` is the
    /// single plain paragraph.
    pub refused: bool,
    /// The guard refused a text after the first, so the first pass's tree was kept: the `\(`
    /// pairs of this source are not math, which a longer text around it may not repeat.
    pub declined: bool,
    /// Block HTML was read, so `deepest` (of this source and every other) decided its room.
    pub block_html: bool,
    /// The first text Ely read for this source (a byte order mark dropped, lone CRs as line
    /// ends, `$$` fences as tildes), the one the guard saw first.
    pub read: Option<String>,
}

/// `source` as the tree `policy.surface` draws.
pub(crate) fn build(source: &str, policy: &mut Policy<'_>) -> MarkdownBlocks {
    let parts = parts(source, policy, Within::default(), false);
    join(parts.nodes, parts.missing)
}

/// The per-block half of [`build`]: everything up to and including the chat links.
#[allow(dead_code)] // `stream` calls `parts` with the place of its part; nothing else builds parts
pub(crate) fn build_parts(source: &str, policy: &mut Policy<'_>) -> Parts {
    parts(source, policy, Within::default(), true)
}

/// Where a source stands in the reply it is a part of, so that built alone it comes out as it
/// does in the whole.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Default)]
struct Within {
    /// The deepest Markdown of the rest of the reply: block HTML nests to what it leaves.
    deepest: usize,
    /// Where the source starts in the reply, for the source offsets the tree keeps.
    offset: usize,
}

fn parts(source: &str, policy: &mut Policy<'_>, within: Within, keep_read: bool) -> Parts {
    let mut missing = Vec::new();
    let mut nodes = vec![rewrite::plain_paragraph(source)];
    let mut refused = true;
    // Ely reads another text than the one written (a byte order mark dropped, lone CRs as line
    // ends, `$$` fences as tildes), and reads `\(` pairs as math in a second pass over swapped
    // text. It asks the guard about each text it is about to parse, so the guard measures what
    // Ely reads, in one parse: a refused first text leaves the plain paragraph, a refused
    // second one keeps the first pass's tree. What depth the Markdown leaves is all block HTML
    // may nest to, wherever it stands (in the rest of the reply too, for a part of one); HTML is
    // read after every text was measured.
    let deepest = Cell::new(0usize);
    let (declined, block_html) = (Cell::new(false), Cell::new(false));
    let (mut read, mut texts) = (None, 0usize);
    let offset = within.offset;
    let parsed = parse_markdown_guarded(
        source,
        &|raw: &str| {
            block_html.set(true);
            let room = MAX_NESTING
                .saturating_sub(deepest.get().max(within.deepest))
                .min(MAX_HTML_NESTING);
            let mut blocks = rewrite::html_block(raw, room)?;
            // The offsets of the tree are moved by `offset` below; what block HTML makes has
            // none, and is moved back by the same amount so that it ends where it began.
            stream::shift(&mut blocks, offset.wrapping_neg());
            Some(blocks)
        },
        &mut |text| {
            texts += 1;
            if keep_read && texts == 1 {
                read = Some(text.to_owned());
            }
            let depth = markdown_depth(text);
            if depth <= MAX_NESTING {
                deepest.set(deepest.get().max(depth));
            } else if texts > 1 {
                declined.set(true);
            }
            depth <= MAX_NESTING
        },
    );
    if let Some(parsed) = parsed {
        // Block HTML nests on top of the Markdown around it: each is under the cap, their
        // sum may not be, and every walk after this one recurses over the tree.
        if tree_depth(&parsed) <= MAX_NESTING {
            let mut kept = parsed;
            if policy.surface == Surface::Preview
                && let Some(inputs) = &policy.diagrams
            {
                kept = rewrite::diagrams(kept, inputs, &mut missing);
            }
            // A failed diagram's note is a quote beside its fence, one level deeper: it counts
            // once it is inserted, and not before.
            if tree_depth(&kept) <= MAX_NESTING {
                nodes = rewrite::pictures(kept, policy);
                if policy.surface == Surface::Chat {
                    rewrite::chat_links(&mut nodes, &mut policy.file_links);
                }
                stream::shift(&mut nodes, offset);
                refused = false;
            } else {
                missing.clear();
            }
        }
    }
    Parts {
        nodes,
        missing,
        deepest: deepest.get(),
        refused,
        declined: declined.get(),
        block_html: block_html.get(),
        read,
    }
}

/// The half of [`build`] that looks across the reply: headings and their slugs, the tables of
/// contents that link to them, the counts and the plain text.
pub(crate) fn join(nodes: Vec<MarkdownBlock>, missing: Vec<DiagramRequest>) -> MarkdownBlocks {
    // The headings are read before the tables of contents that link to them are made:
    // a list of links holds no heading, so the order of the others does not move.
    let headings = headings(&nodes);
    let (nodes, toc) = rewrite::tocs(nodes, &headings);

    let mut kinds = NodeCounts {
        toc,
        ..NodeCounts::default()
    };
    rewrite::each(&nodes, &mut |node| match node {
        MarkdownBlock::Math(_) => kinds.math += 1,
        MarkdownBlock::Paragraph(inline) | MarkdownBlock::Heading(_, inline) => {
            kinds.math += (inline.styles.iter())
                .filter(|(_, style)| *style == Style::Math)
                .count();
        }
        MarkdownBlock::Alert { .. } => kinds.alerts += 1,
        MarkdownBlock::Footnote { .. } => kinds.footnotes += 1,
        MarkdownBlock::Image { .. } => kinds.images += 1,
        MarkdownBlock::Table { .. } => kinds.tables += 1,
        MarkdownBlock::Code { .. } => kinds.code += 1,
        _ => {}
    });

    MarkdownBlocks {
        text: Rc::new(text::plain_text(&nodes)),
        nodes: Rc::from(nodes),
        headings: Rc::from(headings),
        missing_diagrams: missing,
        kinds,
    }
}

/// Every heading the renderer will draw, in the order it draws them (alert bodies and
/// footnotes included), with the anchor each one answers to.
fn headings(nodes: &[MarkdownBlock]) -> Vec<Heading> {
    let mut found = Vec::new();
    let mut seen = HashMap::new();
    rewrite::each(nodes, &mut |node| {
        if let MarkdownBlock::Heading(level, inline) = node {
            found.push(Heading {
                ordinal: found.len(),
                slug: slug(&inline.text, &mut seen).into(),
                title: inline.text.clone().into(),
                depth: usize::from(*level),
            });
        }
    });
    found
}
//! What Sirio does to a parsed tree before it is drawn (design §5.5): block HTML in,
//! diagrams, pictures and links by surface, tables of contents.
//!
//! Every rewrite reaches every depth of the tree (lists, quotes, table cells, alerts,
//! footnotes), because a hostile source can put a picture or a link anywhere.

use ely_gpui_component::documents::{
    AlignKind, Inline, MarkdownBlock as Node, Style, markdown_picture_path,
};
use sirio_diagram::DiagramKind;
use sirio_markdown::{
    Alignment, Block, Document, Inline as Leaf, ListKind, TableCell, expand_html_capped,
};

use super::{DiagramInputs, FileLinkInputs, Heading, Policy, Surface};
use crate::chat::file_links;
use crate::markdown_preview::{DiagramRequest, DiagramState};

// ---- walking ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// The block lists `node` holds, in drawing order: a list's items, a table's head cells
/// then its rows' cells.
pub(super) fn bodies(node: &Node) -> Vec<&[Node]> {
    match node {
        Node::Quote(body) | Node::Footnote { body, .. } | Node::Alert { body, .. } => {
            vec![body]
        }
        Node::List { items, .. } => items.iter().map(|(_, body)| body.as_slice()).collect(),
        Node::Table { head, rows, .. } => head
            .iter()
            .chain(rows.iter().flatten())
            .map(Vec::as_slice)
            .collect(),
        _ => Vec::new(),
    }
}

fn bodies_mut(node: &mut Node) -> Vec<&mut Vec<Node>> {
    match node {
        Node::Quote(body) | Node::Footnote { body, .. } | Node::Alert { body, .. } => {
            vec![body]
        }
        Node::List { items, .. } => items.iter_mut().map(|(_, body)| body).collect(),
        Node::Table { head, rows, .. } => head.iter_mut().chain(rows.iter_mut().flatten()).collect(),
        _ => Vec::new(),
    }
}

fn is_container(node: &Node) -> bool {
    matches!(
        node,
        Node::Quote(_) | Node::List { .. } | Node::Table { .. } | Node::Footnote { .. } | Node::Alert { .. }
    )
}

/// Replaces each node that holds no blocks by what `leaf` makes of it.
fn flat_map(nodes: Vec<Node>, leaf: &mut dyn FnMut(Node) -> Vec<Node>) -> Vec<Node> {
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(nodes.len());
    for mut node in nodes {
        if !is_container(&node) {
            out.extend(leaf(node));
            continue;
        }
        for body in bodies_mut(&mut node) {
            let taken = std::mem::take(body);
            *body = flat_map(taken, leaf);
        }
        out.push(node);
    }
    out
}

/// Visits every node, containers before what they hold.
pub(super) fn each_mut(nodes: &mut [Node], visit: &mut dyn FnMut(&mut Node)) {
    for node in nodes {
        visit(node);
        for body in bodies_mut(node) {
            each_mut(body, visit);
        }
    }
}

/// Visits every node, containers before what they hold.
pub(super) fn each(nodes: &[Node], visit: &mut dyn FnMut(&Node)) {
    for node in nodes {
        visit(node);
        for body in bodies(node) {
            each(body, visit);
        }
    }
}

// ---- small pieces -----------------------------------------------------------------------

/// A picture's width, or none when it is no width: a picture of no size draws as it is.
pub(super) fn clamp_width(width: f32) -> Option<f32> {
    (width.is_finite() && width > 0.0).then_some(width)
}

/// A paragraph of plain `text`.
pub(super) fn plain_paragraph(text: &str) -> Node {
    Node::Paragraph(Inline {
        text: text.to_owned(),
        ..Inline::default()
    })
}

/// A paragraph that is all one link.
fn link_paragraph(text: &str, url: &str) -> Node {
    Node::Paragraph(Inline {
        text: text.to_owned(),
        styles: vec![(0..text.len(), Style::Link)],
        links: vec![(0..text.len(), url.to_owned())],
        ..Inline::default()
    })
}

fn is_web_image(url: &str) -> bool {
    let scheme = |name: &str| {
        url.get(..name.len())
            .is_some_and(|head| head.eq_ignore_ascii_case(name))
    };
    scheme("http://") || scheme("https://")
}

fn is_data_image(url: &str) -> bool {
    url.get(..5)
        .is_some_and(|head| head.eq_ignore_ascii_case("data:"))
}

// ---- block HTML -------------------------------------------------------------------------
